title: Why We Wear Our Watches to Bed

pre.en: What does Gemma's watch do every morning now?
pre.zh: 现在 Gemma 的手表每天早上会做什么？
options: It wakes her up at seven.

intro: 一段电台式的科技小讲解：越来越多的英国人戴着智能手表睡觉。讲的人先给调查数字，再讲手表怎么工作，然后讲一位老师的故事和一位睡眠研究者的看法。读的时候留意说步骤的词：first、then、once、as soon as、until；once、as soon as、until 后面说将来的事也用一般现在时。

sentences.en: Now, here's a number for you.
sentences.zh: 好，先给大家一个数字。

sentences.en: One in four UK adults now wear a smartwatch to bed, according to a survey of 2,000 people.
sentences.zh: 一项针对 2000 人的调查显示，现在每四个英国成年人里，就有一个戴着智能手表睡觉。

sentences.en: They want to see how well they sleep.
sentences.zh: 他们想看看自己睡得怎么样。

sentences.en: And honestly, a watch that tells you how to sleep better sounds too good to be true.
sentences.zh: 说实话，一块能教你怎么睡得更好的手表，听着也太美了，不像真的。

sentences.en: So how does it work?
sentences.zh: 那它是怎么工作的呢？

sentences.en: Well, first, the watch waits until you lie still.
sentences.zh: 首先，手表会等你躺着不动。

sentences.en: Once you stop moving, it starts measuring your heart rate.
sentences.zh: 你一不动，它就开始测你的心率。

sentences.en: It keeps recording until you get up in the morning, and then it gives you a score out of 100.
sentences.zh: 它一直记录到你早上起床，然后给你打个分，满分 100。

sentences.en: Some watches can even tell when you lose your balance and fall over.
sentences.zh: 有些手表甚至能发现你没站稳、摔倒了。

sentences.en: Gemma Ward is a 29-year-old teacher in Leeds, and she's worn hers every night for two years.
sentences.zh: Gemma Ward 是利兹的一名老师，今年 29 岁，她每晚戴着手表睡觉，已经两年了。

sentences.en: "I can't live without it," she told us.
sentences.zh: 「我已经完全离不开它了，」她跟我们说。

sentences.en: She checks her score as soon as she wakes up, before she's even opened her eyes properly.
sentences.zh: 她一醒就看分数，眼睛都还没完全睁开。

sentences.en: At first, she was fascinated by the graphs.
sentences.zh: 一开始，那些图表让她着了迷。

sentences.en: "Buying it seemed like a good idea at the time," she said.
sentences.zh: 「当时觉得买它是个好主意。」她说。

sentences.en: "But now, when I think about sleep, the first thing that comes to mind is a number."
sentences.zh: 「可现在一想到睡觉，我脑子里冒出来的第一个东西就是一个数字。」

sentences.en: Sleep researchers say some people are becoming obsessed with their scores.
sentences.zh: 睡眠研究者说，有些人正变得对分数着了魔。

sentences.en: Dr Alison Hendry, a sleep researcher in Manchester, puts it like this.
sentences.zh: 曼彻斯特的睡眠研究者 Alison Hendry 博士是这么说的：

sentences.en: "If the watch says you've had a bad night, you feel tired, even when you slept well.
sentences.zh: 「手表说你昨晚没睡好，你就觉得累，哪怕你其实睡得不错。

sentences.en: I'd be grateful if people listened to their bodies instead of checking their wrists."
sentences.zh: 我希望大家多听听自己身体的感觉，别老盯着手腕。」

sentences.en: Gemma admits she's often tempted to check the app at 3 am.
sentences.zh: Gemma 承认，她半夜三点也常常忍不住想看一眼 App。

sentences.en: Her watch has even mistaken her for someone asleep while she was watching a long film.
sentences.zh: 有一次她在看一部很长的电影，手表居然把她当成了睡着的人。

sentences.en: So last month, she took it off for a week.
sentences.zh: 所以上个月，她把手表摘了一个星期。

sentences.en: Now she wonders why she started wearing it in the first place.
sentences.zh: 现在她都想不明白，自己当初为什么要戴它。

sentences.en: She slept better without it, she says.
sentences.zh: 她说，不戴反而睡得更好。

sentences.en: And the watch, sitting in a drawer, still sends her a message every morning: "We missed you last night."
sentences.zh: 而那块躺在抽屉里的手表，每天早上还是会给她发一条消息：「昨晚我们想你了。」

cards.note: smart + watch 合成一个词；智能手机 smartphone 也是这样。

cards.zh: 好得令人难以置信（多半有诈）
cards.note: so good that you think there must be a problem with it
读 /ˈmeʒə/；心率是 heart rate。
to become unable to stay standing or sitting steadily, so that you start to fall
cards.tip: your 跟着人称变：lose my / his balance；保持平衡是 keep your balance。
cards.example: I lost my balance on the ice and fell over.

cards.zh: 离不开……；没有……就活不下去
cards.note: to feel that you need something very much and could not manage if you did not have it
cards.tip: 口语里的夸张说法，常说手机、咖啡这类东西；可以换成 couldn't live without sth。
cards.example: I can't live without coffee in the morning.

cards.note: 英式口语常用：I didn't sleep properly（没睡好）。
to be extremely interested in something
at a particular moment in the past, especially when things seemed different from how they seem now
cards.tip: 常暗示「现在看法变了」；别和 at a time（一次、每次）混。
cards.example: It seemed funny at the time, but now I'm a bit embarrassed.

cards.note: if something comes to mind, you suddenly think of it or remember it
cards.tip: 主语是被想起的东西，不是人：Nothing comes to mind。
cards.example: When I think of Paris, the river comes to mind first.

cards.note: 动词、名词 research 重音可前可后；做研究是 do research。
to think about something or someone all the time, more than is normal
cards.tip: 介词用 with；比 be fascinated by 程度更重，常带点「过头了」的意思。读 /əbˈsest/。
cards.example: My brother is obsessed with football.

cards.note: 名词 obsession。
to sleep badly during the night
cards.tip: night 前面的形容词可以换：have a good night / a late night / a sleepless night。
cards.example: Sorry I'm quiet today — I had a bad night.

cards.zh: 如果……我将不胜感激（礼貌请求）
cards.note: a polite way to ask someone to do something, often used in formal emails
w 不发音，读 /rɪst/；手表也叫 wristwatch。
to want to do something, especially something you know you should not do
cards.tip: 后面接动词原形；也可以 be tempted by sth（被……吸引）。
cards.example: I was tempted to leave the meeting early.

cards.zh: 把某人错当成另一个人
cards.note: to think wrongly that one person or thing is another
to remove a piece of clothing, a watch or jewellery from your body
cards.tip: 宾语是代词时放中间：take it off；反义 put sth on。
cards.example: Please take your shoes off at the door.

cards.note: used to talk about the reason why something was done at the beginning
cards.tip: 常放在句尾，带一点「早知道就不……」的意思；列举时 In the first place 是「首先」。
cards.example: Why did you buy it in the first place if you don't like it?

cards.note: 英式读 /drɔː/，和 draw 读音几乎一样。
